title: Concentration, purification and quantification of milk protein residues following cleaning processes using a combination of SPE and RP-HPLC
author: Kürzl, Wohlschläger, et al.
materials: Solvent A (0.1% TFA, 90% ultrapure water and 10% ACN) and solvent B (0.07%TFA, 90% ACN and 10% ultrapure water) are prepared according to Dumpler et al. [10] and used for the RP-HPLC analysis. Furthermore, the solvents A and B are also used during the sample preparation and elution step of the SPE concentration. The guanidine buffer is prepared according to Dumpler et al. [10] containing 6 M guanidine hydrochloride, 21.5 mM trisodium citrate, 19.5 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) and 0.1 M BisTris buffer (pH 6.8).

Protein concentration with the described protocol for SPE results in a total protein recovery of 94.2 ± 3.0% (n = 8). A high reproducibility of the applied SPE method could be proven by a calculation of the standard deviation (3.0%) and the CV (3.2%) of the total protein recovery rate between experiments. Furthermore, the protein recovery rates of the individual milk proteins were calculated and are shown in Fig. 1. Compared to the recovery rate of the total protein concentration, αS1-CN, β-CN, β-LG B and β-LG A achieved higher recovery rates with 102.4 ± 4.3%, 101.9 ± 7.3%, 99.8 ± 9.5% and 97.2 ± 5.0%, respectively. In contrast to that, the recoveries of κ-CN, αS2-CN and α-LA were lower, with 62.5 ± 2.3%, 75.4 ± 8.6% and 85.2 ± 5.8%, respectively.Fig. 1Protein recovery rates after SPE and RP-HPLC for the total protein as well as for the individual milk proteins (κ-CN, αS2-CN, αS1-CN, β-CN, α-LA, β-LG B and β-LG A) (n = 8).Fig 1

steps.title: Prepare solvents and buffer
steps.instruction: Make Solvent A (0.1 % TFA, 90 % ultrapure water, 10 % ACN) and Solvent B (0.07 % TFA, 90 % ACN, 10 % ultrapure water) as described by Dumpler et al.; prepare the guanidine buffer containing 6 M guanidine‑HCl, 21.5 mM trisodium citrate, 19.5 mM DTT and 0.1 M Bis‑Tris, adjust to pH 6.8.

steps.title: Pre‑treat sample
steps.instruction: Filter the sample through a sterile 0.45 µm filter, add 22.67 % (v/v) of a 3 mM Ca(OH)₂ solution and 8 % (v/v) Solvent B, then adjust the pH to 7.0 ± 0.03 using 1 M HCl or 1 M NaOH.

steps.title: Prepare SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Connect the 500 mg C18 SPE cartridge to the vacuum manifold, open the outlet, condition the sorbent with 6 mL ACN (flow < 3.0 mL min⁻¹, slight vacuum allowed), then equilibrate with 6 mL ultrapure water (flow < 3.0 mL min⁻¹). If a pause follows, leave ~1 mL water in the cartridge and keep the outlet closed to avoid drying.

steps.title: Load sample onto SPE
steps.instruction: Apply the prepared sample to the cartridge at a flow rate < 3.0 mL min⁻¹ (do not exceed the cartridge’s binding capacity; recommended protein load 1–6 mg, max ≈5–25 mg).

steps.title: Wash cartridge
steps.instruction: Wash with 100 mL ultrapure water (flow < 6.0 mL min⁻¹, slight vacuum permitted), then apply vacuum and dry the cartridge for 5 min to remove residual water, finally close the outlet.

steps.title: Elute proteins
steps.instruction: Prepare an elution solution of 61.6 % Solvent A and 38.4 % Solvent B. Apply 1.5 mL of this solution to the cartridge, let it soak for 3 min, open the outlet (no vacuum, flow < 3.0 mL min⁻¹) and collect the eluate; afterwards apply vacuum for 15 s to recover remaining elution liquid. Repeat the entire sequence once more (total eluate = 3 mL). Do not reuse the cartridge; verify complete recovery with a 100 µL pipette if needed.

steps.title: Dilute eluate in guanidine buffer
steps.instruction: Mix the collected eluate with the guanidine‑HCl buffer in a 1:2 ratio (one part eluate to two parts buffer), then let the mixture stand at room temperature for 30 min.

steps.title: Perform RP‑HPLC analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 100 µL of the diluted sample onto the RP‑HPLC system (column and gradient as in Dumpler et al.), set the UV detector wavelength to 214 nm, and run the analysis within 24 h of the incubation step.

steps.title: Calibrate RP‑HPLC
steps.instruction: Prepare protein standards in the guanidine buffer: κ‑CN, α‑CN and β‑CN diluted 1:9; α‑LA diluted 1:5; β‑LG B and β‑LG A diluted 1:3. For each standard, inject 5 µL, 10 µL and 20 µL, record peak areas, and construct calibration curves accounting for the purity of each purchased standard.
